title: US Cyclosporiasis Outbreak Update — Aug 28, 2026
summary: CDC's Aug 27 weekly update expands the Taylor Farms/Taco Bell multistate outbreak to 20 states after Georgia, Tennessee, and Texas were added, with confirmed illnesses rising to 11,458 (from 10,930) and hospitalizations to 495 (from 454); the two Michigan deaths are unchanged. Separately, CDC's broader season-wide combined tally across all Cyclospora clusters climbed to 29,024 cases (17,180 lab-confirmed) across 48 states as of Aug 24-25, per Food Safety News and Food Poisoning Bulletin reporting. North Carolina's distinct parsley/cilantro cluster grew to 940 cases and 32 hospitalizations as of Aug 26. Updated KPIs, added three new timeline events, added Georgia/Tennessee/Texas map points and refreshed North Carolina's, and updated the affected case-total claim and NC DHHS quote to reflect current figures.

title: US Cyclosporiasis Outbreak Update — Aug 25, 2026
summary: No new CDC weekly case tally has been published since the Aug 20 figures (10,930 multistate illnesses across 17 states, 454 hospitalizations, 2 deaths; 27,557 combined season-wide), and the outbreak's slowing trend continues to hold. Two new developments emerged: a Chicago couple filed the first Illinois lawsuit against Taylor Farms on Aug 21 over a 23-day delay in diagnosing their cyclosporiasis, and food-safety attorney Bill Marler flagged on Aug 23 that FDA had quietly revised its recalled-lettuce distribution list on Aug 13 to add nine more states and territories (including California, D.C., and Puerto Rico), bringing the total to 40 jurisdictions — none of which had issued their own public notice as of his post. Added a new claims entry on the transparency gap and updated the Walmart recall map point and Bill Marler's quote to reflect the expanded distribution list.

title: US Cyclosporiasis Outbreak Update — Aug 23, 2026
summary: The Taylor Farms/Taco Bell multistate outbreak grew to 10,930 illnesses across 17 states with 454 hospitalizations as of CDC's Aug 20 figures, up from 9,481 on Aug 13. Michigan's cumulative total reached 14,277 cases and 335 hospitalizations, but the state's weekly case increase dropped sharply to 368 (from roughly 1,400 the prior week) — the smallest weekly gain since late June — prompting Michigan's chief medical executive, Dr. Natasha Bagdasarian, to say 'the worst is behind us.' FDA said it has begun onsite inspections and sampling at iceberg lettuce growers in Mexico, expanding beyond its earlier single-facility inspection. Given the slowing case growth and no new states added since Aug 13, the tracker's breaking-news status has been downgraded to reflect the outbreak's transition from acute escalation to a plateauing/declining phase.

title: Tracker Initialized: US Cyclosporiasis Outbreak Backfilled With Full Timeline
summary: Comprehensive historical backfill covering the 2026 U.S. cyclosporiasis outbreak from CDC's May 1 surveillance baseline through the Aug 19 season-wide tally of 15,700+ confirmed cases in 47 states. Includes the Taylor Farms de México/Taco Bell traceback, nationwide lettuce recall, two Michigan deaths, the North Carolina parsley/cilantro cluster, congressional oversight inquiry, and the Mexican regulators' contamination-inspection dispute.
